decisions.quote: Our results replicate those of Lloyd-Fox et al. and confirmed that five-to-eight-month-old infants show cortical specialization for social perception.
decisions.reason: The authors state an explicit overall verdict on the replication as a whole in both the abstract and discussion that their results replicate Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009). Under Rule 1 and the mixed-outcome rules, this overall verdict on the replication as a whole governs over the discussion's observation that the significant differential HbO increase was right-lateralized rather than bilateral.

parent_objection: First reply treats abstract Our results replicate those of Lloyd-Fox et al. as overall verdict. Full Discussion immediately says We thus replicated the findings...However while Lloyd-Fox2009 reported bilateral activation, our effect only significant in right hemisphere, then says lateralization analysis marginal and no strong conclusions. Codebook explicitly says opening confirmation of focal effect does not outweigh a tested-original contrast unless truly overall verdict on whole replication. Decide whether lateralization is an explicitly contrasted re-tested finding (mixed), a non-conclusive incidental observation authors do not treat as replication failure (successful), or evidence insufficient. Do not decide merely by significance or treat any use of replicate as overall. Read actual original-specific discussion/abstract and main claim. State how codebook hierarchy applies.

blind_target.authors: Lloyd-Fox S., Blasi A., Volein A., Everdell N., Elwell C.E., Johnson M.H.
blind_target.title: Social perception in infancy: a near infrared spectroscopy study.
blind_target.evidence_quote: In the present study, we aim to replicate the results of  Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009)  and investigate the impact of infant  Negative Affect  (as measured by parental questionnaire) on the early cortical specialization for processing social dynamic stimuli. To this end, we used a similar fNIRS paradigm and the same stimuli as used previously by  Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009, Experiment 2) .
blind_target.outcome_quote: We thus replicated the findings of  Lloyd-Fox et al.’s study (2009) . However, while  Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009)  reported bilateral activation in five-month olds, the HbO increase we observed for social-dynamic compared to non-social dynamic stimuli was only significant in the right hemisphere.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm differential activation but explicitly contrast their right-only significant activation with the original bilateral finding; this is an agreeing and a differing comparison under rule 2.
